init.title: Connection mode

data_description.connection_mode: Local relay keeps the Schluter app working. Local only takes the thermostat off the cloud completely, so the Schluter app shows it offline. Switching between the two local modes needs no DNS change.

local.title: Required: add a DNS record
local.description:
Local control only works once your thermostat looks up **{hostname}** and gets this Home Assistant host's IP address. Add this record on your router or DNS server:

**{hostname}  →  {ip}**

Also make sure:
- this Home Assistant host has a fixed IP address,
- the thermostat can reach it on TCP port {port}.

After saving, power-cycle the thermostat so it picks up the new address; it reconnects within a few minutes. To undo, switch back to Cloud and delete the record. Step-by-step instructions: {docs_url}

data_description.acknowledge: Without the record the thermostat keeps talking to the cloud and Home Assistant shows it as unavailable.

error.must_acknowledge: Add the DNS record first, then tick the box.
error.dns_not_detected: This Home Assistant host doesn't resolve the name to its own IP yet. If you just added the record, or Home Assistant uses a different DNS server than your thermostat, this can be fine: select Submit again to continue.
error.dns_still_local: Your DNS record for local control is still in place, so in Cloud mode the thermostat would keep looking for Home Assistant and stay offline. Delete the record and power-cycle the thermostat. Select Submit again to switch now.

options.relay: Local relay (advanced, needs a DNS record)
options.local: Local only (advanced, needs a DNS record)

local_not_connected.title: Thermostat hasn't connected to Home Assistant
local_not_connected.description:
Local control is on, but no thermostat has connected to Home Assistant's gateway. This almost always means the DNS record is missing or isn't reaching the thermostat.

Check that **{hostname}** resolves to **{ip}** on your network, that the thermostat can reach that IP on TCP port {port}, then power-cycle the thermostat. To go back to the cloud, open the integration's Configure menu and choose Cloud.

This message clears on its own when the thermostat connects.

gateway_port_in_use.message: Could not start the local gateway on port {port}; is something else using it? ({error})
